summary: VizPilot (Nanyang Technological University; IEEE VIS 2026) is a browser extension that uses GPT-5 to reverse-engineer SVG composite data visualizations into atomic explanation units, binds each unit to SVG DOM selectors, and presents them as a guided scrollytelling tour plus free exploration. It is evaluated by manual inspection of four visualizations across input modalities, an LLM-judge robustness check on 18 gallery examples, and a 16-person within-subjects study against static text descriptions. The 'onboarding' is for readers of charts, not software developers.

claims.claim: VizPilot reduces users' cognitive load and speeds comprehension relative to a text baseline.
claims.evidence: §6.4.1: task accuracy at ceiling in both conditions (3.62 vs 3.75 of 4), so comprehension is not shown to differ. Completion time 262.9s -> 194.4s (Wilcoxon p=0.039, n=16, no multiple-comparison correction). NASA-TLX and PSSUQ are large but subjective, and the authors note novelty effects. The baseline is static paper text with no highlighting, so medium and content are confounded.

claims.claim: The pipeline is robust across all four composite design patterns.
claims.evidence: Table 3: decomposition F1 0.92-0.97 and E2E 0.83-0.94 on 18 author-curated gallery visualizations, scored by an LLM-as-judge panel (GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet). Low-confidence cases (5/18) were escalated to the authors. No human ground-truth agreement for the judges is reported.

claims.claim: Each input modality (SVG, image, interaction code) is essential.
claims.evidence: §6.1, Table 2: qualitative manual inspection of four visualizations; no quantitative scores.

patterns.note: Guided, element-highlighted walkthrough vs static text saved about 68s on two charts for 16 students, with accuracy at ceiling. This concerns chart-reader onboarding, not developer comprehension of code or domain.
Design analogue only: the MLLM proposes explanation-to-element links that are then programmatically verified against the SVG DOM before display. Not requirement-to-code traceability.
A three-model LLM-judge panel with confidence-based human escalation is used for the gallery evaluation; the judges are not validated against human labels.

methodology.sample: 4 visualizations (modality analysis), 18 gallery visualizations (LLM-judged), 16 participants on 2 visualizations (MatrixWave, PrettiSmart) with 4 questions each.
methodology.baselines: Static text descriptions from the original papers. No comparison with existing onboarding tools (D-Tour, DashGuide, LEVA).
methodology.models: GPT-5 for generation; GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude 3.5 Sonnet as judges.
methodology.variance: SDs reported for user-study measures; none for the pipeline.
methodology.contamination_controls: none; the gallery visualizations are published systems likely present in training data.
methodology.languages: SVG/D3/Vega-Lite web visualizations; not applicable to code.

standards.artifacts: Online example gallery only; no code, prompts or study data released.

biases.detail: Visualization literacy and chart onboarding; no software-development or coding-agent content.
Static paper text vs an interactive highlighted tour; no competing onboarding system.
Gallery robustness numbers come from LLM judges plus author review of escalations.

coi.detail: Academic authors. Some study visualizations (e.g. PrettiSmart, PonziLens) may come from the senior author's own prior work, which is a minor self-selection issue.

verdict_reason: Off-topic: onboarding readers to data visualizations, not developers to code or domains. Its evidence is also weak (n=16, ceiling accuracy, strawman text baseline, unvalidated LLM-judge robustness numbers).
applicability: Does not transfer as evidence. The design idea worth noting for a developer walkthrough feature is that the LLM proposes explanation steps but every step's anchor is checked deterministically before it is shown. For code walkthroughs that would mean each step cites a file and line or symbol that the harness verifies exists. This paper does not test that for code.
